title: Typography / Large-format scale — 4x table

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: 4x

slide_intent: Increase type and line spacing together for larger viewing conditions, because enlargement should preserve hierarchy rather than merely stretch individual headings.
strategic_value: A ready-made 4x table can keep IBM large-format typography related to the baseline scale and its script adjustments.
demonstration: The selected 4x tab shows default sizes 24–1200, 95% adjusted sizes and corresponding line heights. The source repeats the 1072/1018.4/1184 row; the capture preserves it.
practical_value: Use the 4x values only for a format that the surrounding guidance assigns that multiplier, then choose the relevant script column.

content_islands.name: Scaled type columns
content_islands.spec: Pair each default size with its 95% adjusted equivalent.

content_islands.name: Scaled line heights
content_islands.spec: Keep line-height alternatives aligned with their size rows, including the repeated source row near the bottom.

ingredient.name: 4x large-format type scale
ingredient.role: Preserve apparent hierarchy at a larger format or viewing distance.
ingredient.application: Use the supplied 4x type and line-height values where the medium’s guidance calls for 4x; retain the 95% point-size adjustment for the named scripts.
ingredient.scope: The parent guidance gives large posters/small signage and 8K digital artboards as 4x examples and assumes artwork at 100%. The repeated 1072 row is a source duplication, not a new scale step.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying large-format guidance explains that viewing distance changes perceived type size.
reference_purposes.Application: The 4x table provides multiplied size and line-height values without requiring manual calculation.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying guidance conditions these large-format rules on artwork produced at 100%; other design scales require additional scaling.
